Week 9 is underway, and we're tracking all of the injuries before game time.

The San Francisco 49ers are expected to be without wide receivers Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring). General manager John Lynch said on KNBR that receivers Demarcus Robinson and KhaDarel Hodge will be available. The hope was both Evans and Samuel would be back after the 49ers' Week 8, but it appears they will be out for Sunday's home game against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice Thursday, but told reporters afterward that he’ll “be good” to play Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles. Running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) also wasn’t on the field, putting his availability in doubt. Devin Singletary and Greg Derosiers Jr. would serve as the top two running backs if the second-year Arizona State back cannot go.

Other Week 9 injuries to monitor:

  • Shedeur Sanders will likely be the Cleveland Browns' starter Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. Quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) missed practiced this week and remains in protocol. Sanders has not started a game since Week 18 of last season.

  • While the New York Jets will get Breece Hall (quad) back after a five-game absence, wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) is out for the team's road game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Wilson entered protocol after taking a hit to the head during last week's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders. He reported experiencing symptoms when he reported to the team's practice facility on Monday.

  • Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons will not play this week, but did return to practice for the first time since tearing his ACL and meniscus in his left knee last season. He is eyeing a Thanksgiving Eve game comeback against the Los Angeles Rams on Nov. 25.

  • Emeka Egbuka (foot) has a chance to take the field in Chicago against the Bears in Week 9. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver was a full participant in practice on Thursday after missing the past two weeks with a concussion and a foot injury.

item.title: Week 9 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our 5 best bets for this week's games
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 9 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 9 of the NFL season began with the Jacksonville Jaguars cruising to a 33-10 win on the road against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday night. Rain played a factor, but Ravens QB Joe Fagnano had a tough debut and there wasn’t much suspense about the final outcome.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 9 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Cincinnati Bengals (-3, 52.5) at Atlanta Falcons

Pond: Death, taxes and Mike Gesicki touchdowns.

The first two are sure things. The third is inching closer to becoming a guarantee.

Gesicki has accumulated a respectable 17 catches for 241 yards for the surging Bengals (5-2), who are in the midst of a three-game winning streak entering Sunday’s showdown with the Falcons at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid.

While those stats are solid, it’s what Gesicki has done in the red zone that’s turning heads. He has scored six touchdowns, including one in five consecutive games, meaning 35% of his catches this season have gone for scores.

Gesicki has been Burrow’s favorite target all season in the red zone and I don’t see that changing here just because they’re playing Atlanta on another continent. Four of Gesicki’s touchdowns have come via receptions of 15 yards or less.

Bet: TE Mike Gesicki anytime touchdown (+230, FanDuel)

New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs (-10, 47.5)

Russell: If there’s a close game to blow, Aaron Glenn and the Jets are ready and willing to give it away. Luckily, when it comes to betting on New York, winning (or coming all that close) isn’t required here. It’s a particularly convenient situation, as they play a team known for winning close games but not covering big numbers, even at their best. 

Kansas City was “back” after a pair of home prime-time games had a fresh Patrick Mahomes running around, Travis Kelce in wedding shape and a crop of interesting wide receivers to support a passing game that was allowed to take a backseat to Andy Reid’s brand-new toy, Kenneth Walker. With that visibility in the comfy confines of Arrowhead, the Chiefs’ market rating raised and held its position just below the top teams in the NFL. 

Since then, the Chiefs outgained the Dolphins by 5 yards in a point spread cover, barely fended off the Raiders and joined the club in outlasting the meek Chargers. Now, having lost back-to-back games to two good teams on the road, they have a thin receiver room, a banged-up Kelce and Walker’s yardage on a decline. Yet, they’re squished in-between the Jaguars and Patriots in THE WINDOW’s estimated market ratings. 

Just three weeks ago, New England was -7 at home to the Jets, in a game that pushed against the spread. New York lost two more games as a home favorite, and the market has adjusted the Jets down in accordance. 

In that time, the Jets have arguably the worst pass defense in the NFL, but the Chiefs haven’t shown that’s something they can exploit. Meanwhile, New York’s offense has crept up the advanced metrics with their pass-catching corps filling out with healthy returns Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Michell and Mason Taylor, and Braelon Allen making Breece Hall seemingly expendable. 

Getting David Bailey (groin) back this week would help the Jets defense, especially with the Chiefs’ offensive line susceptible to the pass rush with Justin Simmons’ (IR) replacement, Khalil Benson, a far better run-blocker than pass-protector. 

Nevertheless, with L’Jarius Sneed out, and Mansoor Delane questionable, the Jets should be able to move the ball well enough to keep this game close. 

Bet: Jets +10 (-110, BetMGM)

Dallas Cowboys (-6, 51.5) at Indianapolis Colts

Jacob: You’re aware of the phrase “The more things change, the more they stay the same?” Well, let me introduce you to the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, who once again are all offense, no defense.

Dallas arrives in Indianapolis averaging 27.4 points per game (seventh most in the NFL) and allowing 26.6 PPG (sixth most in the NFL). Mirroring recent seasons, the Cowboys field an offense that’s entirely reliant on QB Dak Prescott and a stop unit that stops, well, nothing. Just look at the rankings: ninth in passing offense, 25th in rushing offense, 22nd in passing defense, dead last in rushing defense.

All of this explains why the over has cashed in six of Dallas’ eight games this season (including final scores of 37-20, 34-31, 34-30, 38-21 and 33-30). And why the over is 37-16-1 in Cowboys games going back to Week 13 of the 2023 season.

Since last season kicked off, the Cowboys and their opponents have combined for more than 50 points in 17 of 25 games, including eight of 13 on the road.

By now, it’s pretty clear where I’m heading with this wager. But of course it usually takes two to tango when betting a total. Good news: I’m quite confident the Colts will bring their dancing shoes Sunday, as they’ve eclipsed the total in five of eight games, including three of the last four.

Indy’s defense has been particularly putrid this year, with the Jaguars (42 points last week), Ravens (41), Steelers (34), Chiefs (33) and Titans (26) all lighting up the scoreboard.

Bet: Cowboys-Colts over 51.5 (-108, BetMGM)

Denver Broncos (-2.5, 43.5) at Carolina Panthers

Jacob: Broncos rookie RB Jonah Coleman has only played in three of his team’s first eight games. And he wasn’t overly impressive in any of them. He had 39 yards on 10 carries against Jacksonville in Week 2; 54 yards on nine carries against Arizona two weeks ago; and 41 yards on 11 totes against Kansas City last week.

Here’s the thing, though: Coleman surpassed his rushing prop projection in all three contests. And the fourth-round pick from Washington did it against defenses that currently rank No. 1 (Jaguars), No. 8 (Chiefs) and No. 19 (Arizona) in stopping the run.

This week, Coleman faces Carolina, which is yielding 140.7 rushing yards per game and 4.83 yards per carry, figures that respectively rank 30th and 28th in the NFL. And that’s after the Panthers held Green Bay — which has by far the NFL’s most anemic running game — to 66 yards on 26 carries last week.

In the previous game, Tampa Bay backfield mates Bucky Irving (106 yards), Kenneth Gainwell (88 yards) and Sean Tucker (52 yards) shredded Carolina for 246 rushing yards on 45 carries. Other running backs to light up the Panthers this season: Cleveland’s Quinshon Judkins (70 yards), Atlanta’s Bijan and Brian Robinson (72 and 51 yards, respectively) and Chicago’s D’Andre Swift (124 yards) and Kyle Monangai (100 yards).

Coleman has been Denver’s leading ball carrier and rusher in all three games he’s played. He’ll do that again Sunday and easily eclipse 60 yards.

Bet: Jonah Coleman over 52.5 rushing yards (-114, FanDuel)

Buffalo Bills (-3, 45.5) at Minnesota Vikings

Pond: Big news dropped Thursday when Minnesota announced that QB Carson Wentz would start Monday’s showdown against Buffalo.

That might sound crushing for the Vikings (6-1), who are coming off their first loss of the season following a 19-15 road setback against Detroit. However, Murray has been anything but spectacular under center this season. He has thrown for just 1,022 yards (27th), and five touchdowns.

Now, Minnesota turns to Wentz, which isn’t such a bad thing. With Murray sidelined to start the season, Wentz led the Vikings to big wins against NFC rivals Green Bay and Chicago before heading back to clipboard duties.

And one of the players who Wentz targeted during his two-game run was T.J. Hockenson.

The standout tight end hauled in a combined seven passes on nine targets for 65 yards, highlighted by a 16-yard TD catch in the season-opening win over the Packers.

More recently, Hockenson has been fantastic in a more featured role in the Minnesota offense. Over the past two outings, he has eight catches on 10 targets for 93 yards. He also recorded touchdowns in both contests.

Wentz will be looking for familiar, trustworthy faces when Minnesota gets in the red zone and Hockenson – along with Justin Jefferson – will be one of those faces.

Back the former first-round pick out of Iowa to make three games in a row with a touchdown.

Bet: TE T.J. Hockenson anytime TD (+250, BetMGM)

item.content:encoded:
We're officially into Week 9 of the NFL season (and the looming NFL trade deadline), where teams will have to make a decision on the intended course of the remainder of their season — are they going all in? Or is it time to tear it all down and look toward the future?

After falling to 4-5 on Thursday night, the Baltimore Ravens finalized a trade for Jacoby Brissett as they look to salvage their season. The team officially placed Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve this week, and undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano looked like … well, an undrafted free agent in his first career start. He completed 10 of 18 pass attempts for 60 yards and two touchdowns to open up Week 9 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, with a 22.7 NFL passer rating. Despite Brissett's struggles this year, there's no doubt he'll be a welcome upgrade.

NFL fans also await news on the fate of star running back Jonathan Taylor, who has been touted as a potential trade-deadline mover as the Indianapolis Colts kicked off their franchise reset with a fire sale. They've already traded away two foundational players, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, for several draft picks as they look to the future, leaving us to wonder whether their star running back could be next.

item.title: NFL predictions: Fireworks between Falcons and Bengals
item.description: The Falcons need a victory to stay afloat in the playoff hunt, but can it come against this Bengals team?
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons squandered a golden opportunity to take control of the NFC South in Week 8, falling completely flat in a bad weather game against the Bucs. Now sitting at 3-5—along with the rest of the division—Atlanta is in a difficult place. Games against some of the AFC and NFC’s best await over the next month, sandwiched around the team’s Week 11 bye.

The first game in this sequence comes early Sunday morning in Madrid, as the Falcons take on the Bengals. Cincinnati is a bit volatile, but possesses one of the best offenses in the NFL led by quarterback Joe Burrow and the elite receiver duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Right now, the Falcons are 3-point underdogs against the Bengals, per FanDuel. Atlanta needs a victory to stay afloat in the playoff hunt, but can it come against this Cincinnati team? Let’s take a closer look.

Falcons vs Bengals Week 9 predictions

The Bengals hold the NFL’s second-best scoring offense, best third-down offense, and are also top-10 in total yardage. This will be one of the biggest tests for Atlanta’s defense all season. The good news for the Falcons is that Cincinnati’s offense is very one-dimensional, with the vast majority of their production coming via the passing game. Over the past few weeks, Atlanta’s biggest issue has been stopping the run.

That shouldn’t be a problem in Week 9, as the Bengals are 30th in rushing yardage and 28th in yards per carry. So all eyes then turn to the Falcons ability to slow down Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. I’m not sure how well the Falcons will fare, but having their full complement of cornerbacks available will be a big help. A.J. Terrell, C.J. Henderson, and Billy Bowman are back in the lineup together for the first time since September.

Joe Burrow has been fantastic, but he’s still vulnerable to pressure. With the Falcons (hopefully) getting star edge rusher James Pearce Jr. back in the lineup this weekend, the pass rush is the best path to victory. Atlanta has been outstanding generating interior pressure and pretty solid outside, but has lacked a true finisher to pile up sacks. Pearce brings that ability, and will hopefully bring a big boost to the defensive line on passing downs.

On the other side of the ball, the message is simple: the Falcons offense must get back on track, and can’t afford to start slow. Michael Penix Jr. is coming off a career-worst performance in a monsoon against the Bucs. The Bengals defense has been opportunistic and good at limiting scoring, but gives up a ton of yardage. This will be the softest defense the Falcons have faced in weeks, and they must take advantage.

Atlanta will need a good day from Penix and the passing game to keep pace with Burrow, but the biggest player to watch is probably Bijan Robinson. This game has the potential to be a “Bijan takeover” performance, with Cincinnati 29th in yards per carry allowed on defense. Bijan got a bit stuck in the mud against Tampa Bay, and I think he’ll have an explosive game in Madrid.

All in all, it likely comes down to the Falcons ability to limit the Bengals offensive chances by holding the ball as much as possible, and capitalizing on their own scoring opportunities. Cincinnati is beatable—the game last week against the Titans showed that—but you have to be able to keep up with them offensively. This is a perfect bounce-back opportunity for Michael Penix, Bijan Robinson, and the offense as a whole.

item.title: 2027 Bears mock draft: Post-Jeffery Simmons trade picks
item.description: WCG’s lead draft analyst @jacobinfante24 shares his latest 2027 Bears mock draft after the Jeffery Simmons trade.
item.content:encoded:
If you’ve been a Bears fan for long enough, you know the drill by now. The 2027 NFL Draft figures to be another year where they don’t have a first-round pick, having traded their first-rounder this year and in 2028 to the Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

I say this not to disagree with the trade; I’m highly in favor of it, and Simmons was absolutely dominant in his debut when the Bears beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks on Monday. But in years past, Chicago has entered drafts without first-round picks multiple times, thanks in part to trades the team has made for players like Jay Cutler, Khalil Mack, and Justin Fields.

Barring an unforeseen trade for a first-round pick, the Bears won’t make their first pick in 2027 until Day 2, where they currently sit near the bottom of the second round for their first selection of that weekend. That makes projecting prospects to Chicago in mock drafts a little more difficult, as it requires a deeper level of research than the surface level of having to know which top-ten prospect might end up on the team.

Luckily for you guys, I have you covered. Here is my first Bears mock draft after the Jeffery Simmons trade, for which I used the PFN mock draft simulator to generate the picks for the other 31 NFL teams.

Round 2: Zabien Brown, CB, Alabama

Now that the Bears have a superstar at defensive tackle, their biggest need on the roster is arguably at cornerback. It’s likely they see a different group at the position in 2027, too; Jaylon Johnson could be released to free up significant cap space, and Tyrique Stevenson arguably hasn’t shown enough consistency to earn a long-term extension as he approaches impending free agency next offseason. To pair up with Kyler Gordon and Malik Muhammad, Chicago will need to bring in a new cornerback.

An intelligent and scrappy cornerback, Zabien Brown is a quick processor who acts upon his diagnoses in coverage with impressive urgency and ideal physicality at the catch point. He’s a willing and capable tackler who’s sticky in man coverage and understands his assignments well in zone coverage. He doesn’t stand out as elite in an aspect of his game, which drops him to Day 2 for me, but he’s a well-rounded cornerback with a strong game who could be a good starting cornerback for years to come.

Round 3: Mateen Ibirogba, DT, Texas Tech

After trading for Simmons, the Bears definitely have a stronger defensive tackle room than they did going into the regular season. However, Grady Jarrett stands out as a potential cap casualty this coming offseason, and they don’t have a true standout alongside Simmons on the roster currently. It wouldn’t be surprising at all if they use another early-round draft pick on an interior defender.

Mateen Ibirogba was originally an edge rusher at Georgetown who eventually bulked up to play defensive tackle, excelled and transferred to Wake Forest, where he would continue to excel before earning a presumably hefty NIL sum to go to Texas Tech. His previous EDGE experience shows in his pass-rushing chops, as he’s an explosive interior defender with impressive get-off speed and a deep arsenal of push-pulls, cross-chops, and club-swims needed to shed blocks. Though his anchor against the run is average, he has legitimate upside as an interior rusher on passing downs.

Round 5 (via Falcons): Antwan Raymond, RB, Rutgers

As good as the Bears’ offense currently is, I don’t think I could imagine Ben Johnson going one whole draft without securing another skill position player. Roschon Johnson is currently in the last year of his rookie contract, and in the carries we’ve seen him have over the last few weeks with Kyle Monangai injured, he doesn’t seem to have the decisiveness in between the tackles or the explosiveness to warrant another contract. This could make Chicago look for a new third-string running back in 2027.

I see Antwan Raymond developing into a high-end backup or a decent spot starter at running back, which is good value in Round 5. He has a low center of gravity and makes precise movements in the open field, taking sharp angles to open running lanes and making smart cuts to evade defenders. He plays with ideal patience and tempo variance out of the backfield, and he’s also a willing and physical pass protector. Though his breakaway speed isn’t elite and could limit his big-play potential, he has enough short-area quickness and agility to make up for it.

Round 6: Tobi Osunsanmi, EDGE, Indiana

How the Bears approach the defensive end position and what archetype of player they look for could depend on how they address this offseason. Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat are two potential cap casualties who would free up a ton of cap space, but Odeyingbo looked good before getting hurt, and Sweat is coming off of his best performance of the year in Week 8. If they keep both, they could look to throw a speed rusher into the mix as depth.

As of this writing, Tobi Osunsanmi leads the Big Ten with 10.0 sacks and 15.0 tackles for loss through his first nine games with Indiana. He’s a little smaller than the typical Dennis Allen edge rusher at 6’2” and 250 pounds, and he had a season-ending injury to close out 2025 at Kansas State. But he’s a twitchy edge rusher with good bend at the top of his arc, a high motor in pursuit, and proper hand activity needed to stack and shed blocks at the point of attack.

Round 7: Aidan Banfield, OG, North Carolina

With a seventh-round pick, you’re really only looking for depth options. If you can get a good long-term backup out of this pick, it would be tremendous value. The Bears have drafted at least one offensive lineman every single year that Ryan Poles has been their general manager, and I don’t see that trend stopping in 2027.

Aidan Banfield is only a junior, so there’s no guarantee he declares for this year’s draft. However, the three-sport high school athlete is explosive coming off the line of scrimmage and demonstrates good mobility changing direction against stunts and inside speed rushes along the interior. He demonstrates ideal spatial awareness in pass protection and can execute double-team and chip block assignments well, too. Once he gets to the NFL, he’ll need to get stronger and work on his pad level, but there’s potential for him to be a very good backup in the pros.

item.title: Lions vs. Dolphins: 3 key matchups
item.description: Our Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins preview identifies three key matchups.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions (5-2) take their talents to South Beach to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). Fresh off a three-game win streak, including two in a row against the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings, the Lions have reestablished themselves as true NFC North contenders.

Despite the back-to-back-to-back victories, the Lions still find themselves currently in third place in the division. This week, the Chicago Bears take on the rising Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Minnesota Vikings host Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on “Monday Night Football.” If the Lions take care of their business, there is a realistic opportunity that Dan Campbell’s team will sit alone at the top of the standings.

From just about every performance and talent metric, the Lions should have the edge in this matchup. But digging deeper, the Dolphins are rebuilding in a way that should remind Lions fans of the Dan Campbell led 2021 team.

In what could typically be labeled a “trap game,” often the NFL rears its powerful element of parity into the equation. To avoid that, the key matchups will come down to not necessarily the talent on the field, the grit of the players to determine the ultimate outcome.

Let’s dive in to the three key matchups centered on the intangible traits that will make or break Sunday’s matchup in south Florida.

Gritty rookies in key roles

Breaking the normal structure of the article here as this first key matchup really is not a direct positional or players matchup, but the comparative play of the key rookies on each team. While many readers here at Pride of Detroit are familiar the Grit Index, for newer readers, it is the NFL Draft metric that Erik Schlitt and I have created to grade prospects on their intangible qualities.

In the 2026 NFL Draft, seven teams drafted players in the elite tier of the Grit Index with a score of 9+. The Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins were two of those teams.

For the Lions, it was Blake Miller, Keith Abney, and Skyler Gill-Howard. For the Dolphins, it was Jacob Rodriguez and Michael Taaffe.

You could call it coincidence, but I am not surprised that each of these five rookies have become key contributors for their respective teams. In fact, Rodriguez and Taaffe are first and second, respectively, in snaps played on the entire Dolphins roster. Similarly, Miller, Abney, and Gill-Howard lead the Lions 2026 rookie draft class in snap counts on the season.

They key here with all five of these players is which one will either rise to the occasion, or which one will be a potential liability? Rookies go through growing pains and not all progress is linear. Will Taaffe rise to the occasion against the Lions elite offensive weapons? Will Rodriguez command and communicate the defense to his teammates as the green dot linebacker against the creatively-detailed Lions offense run by offensive coordinator Drew Petzing and Jared Goff?

Will the Lions rookies take their strong starts to the next level, or will it be a game filled with growing pains coming off a three-game win streak?

The play of these rookies will go a long way in determining the outcome of the game.

The Lions’ linebacker room

This is a big week. At this point, we’re all aware of and have been in the emotional waiting room following the updates and progression after Jack Campbell’s traumatic neck injury against the Vikings. The impact, though, is most significantly felt by those players closest to him.

The key matchup is not how fellow linebackers Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Trevor Nowaske fill in Jack Campbell’s shoes, no player will be able to do that for this team. And I don’t suspect they are trying to.

The key is how Barnes, Rodriguez, and Nowaske can play as the best version of themselves and as a unit while battling this adversity on and off the field.

In my view, having Kelvin Sheppard as defensive coordinator, former linebacker coach, and former linebacker himself, he is in a unique position to lead these players through this storm. Sheppard has expressed nothing but confidence in the group.

“I raised these other guys that are about to play. Malcolm Rodriguez and Derrick Barnes, those are my little brothers and they know the standard. They both have worn the green dot before. So, this isn’t like a first-time ordeal for either one of them, because that load might get shared. We’re still working through that, but I’m confident in either one of them.”

I don’t expect this group to be perfect as each player adapts to their adjusted roles. But I do expect each to play with passion and grit. I expect them to prepare and play like 46.

Zach Sieler vs. Lions interior offensive line

Lastly, turning to the leader of the Dolphins, captain Zach Sieler is not only the fins most disruptive player on defense, he is the heart and soul of the team.

Dan Campbell has emphasized Sieler’s impact.

“Defensively, Sieler’s really the anchor in there. You know, he’s played good football for a really long time, man. Smart, crafty, powerful, can get an edge in the pass game.”

Relentless in both the run and pass game, Sieler will present a challenge to the youth of the Lions interior offensive line. With starting center Cade Mays not practicing and a wave of injuries on defense, the Lions can control the game if Christian Mahogany, Juice Scruggs, and Tate Ratledge can continue to win the line of scrimmage along the interior.

In a game where, On Paper, the Lions have a distinct advantage, players like Sieler can lead the charge in a spoiler’s effort.

Three key matchups. Three opportunities for grit to win the day.

item.title: Ravens were down to their third QB and had a predictably ugly performance in blowout loss to Jaguars
item.description: The Ravens had to prepare for Thursday night with their top two QBs on injured reserve.
item.content:encoded:
It was sad watching the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday night. 

The Ravens were a Super Bowl contender not long ago. Many thought they could bounce back from a bad year and be a top team again this season. It's a reason they were scheduled for a prime-time game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. But Lamar Jackson got hurt early this season, then got hurt again last Sunday, and Tyler Huntley got hurt too. 

That left the Ravens to play undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, their third quarterback, on Thursday night. He played through an injured ankle and ended up having to deal with a rainstorm most of the night. He was the Ravens' only option left, and the results were predictable. The Jaguars caught the Ravens at the right time and had an easy night in a 33-10 win. The Ravens finished with 57 yards passing.

The Ravens (4-5) have decisions to make before the trade deadline. They are reportedly on the verge of dealing for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and while that will make them a functional offense, it's unlikely Brissett saves the season. Jackson might return from a right thumb injury but that's no guarantee, and the Ravens might be well out of the race by the time he is healed anyway. 

Thursday night was an uncompetitive, bad game. The Jaguars (6-2) are clearly one of the best teams in the NFL this season, but practically any team would have defeated Baltimore on Thursday night. There wasn't anything the Ravens or Fagnano could do, no matter how many tricks they had in the game plan. It was an unwinnable situation, which might be the case for the rest of their season too. 

Ravens try to get tricky

The Ravens opened in a wildcat formation with Derrick Henry getting the first snap of the game at quarterback. There were more wildcat plays, extra linemen and any other tricks the Ravens could figure out. Henry even had a pass completion on the first drive. 

No amount of trickery was saving the Ravens. The Jaguars are a good team with a strong defense and Baltimore couldn't move the ball. The rain didn't help. Baltimore had 27 yards passing in the first half. Its longest completion was 7 yards and its longest play was 9 yards in the first two quarters.

Baltimore was trying to stay in it until Jacksonville hit a big play late in the half. Against a blitz, Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington downfield, and he was in the clear to run for a 50-yard touchdown. Lawrence had 197 passing yards in the first half, more than six times what his counterpart Fagnano had at halftime. 

Washington's touchdown made the score 17-3. It's hard to count an NFL team out with a half to go, but it was hard to believe Baltimore would score 14 more points, much less outscore Jacksonville by 14. 

Jaguars pull away

Coming out of halftime, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter optimistically told Amazon Prime Video he wanted to see his offense score on the first drive and see what happened after that. The Ravens threw an interception on the first drive. 

The Ravens were trailing 20-3 when they got a break, as Travis Hunter fumbled and Baltimore recovered near midfield. But the Ravens couldn't get a first down, and on fourth-and-inches tight end Mark Andrews, lined up for what looked like a tush push, fumbled the snap. It looked like he was going to turn and hand it off but it didn't matter because he couldn't hold onto the ball. 

It was that kind of night. The Jaguars caused some of those issues too. Their defense is very good, and the offense is capable of putting up a lot of points if there's not a downpour of rain. They have a good chance of making a deep playoff run. 

The same could have been said about the Ravens before Jackson's latest injury. Brissett will be an upgrade over what we saw against the Jaguars, but there was a reason he was demoted to third string by Arizona this week and then was available in a trade. The Ravens' season probably isn't going anywhere. Things could look even worse in Baltimore by Tuesday's trade deadline.

item.title: Desmond Howard, Reggie White and more highlight Packers’ best moments against Patriots
item.description: The Packers have a short but interesting history with the New England Patriots.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots are the epitome of what good ol’ Mike McCarthy would have called an “uncommon opponent.” They’ve been around for more than 50 years, but the Packers have only encountered them 13 times, and that counts their matchup in Super Bowl XXXI.

But there’s still no shortage of big statistical performances on the Packers’ side of these matchups, and, as always, looking back gives us a great chance to Remember Some Guys. And that remembering takes us all the way from the unremarkable days of the late 1980s to the Super Bowl and beyond.

Most passing yards – 368 (Aaron Rodgers, 2014)

Aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady squared off exactly once when both teams were at anything resembling full strength, and it was a game for the ages. Aaron Rodgers barbecued the Patriots’ secondary to the tune of 368 yards and two touchdowns, including a magnificent 45-yard catch and run by Jordy Nelson just before halftime.

Most rushing yards – 136 (Ahman Green, 2002)

The Packers traveled to New England on a rainy October day in 2002 to face off against the defending Super Bowl champs and came away with a convincing 28-10 win. Ahman Green fueled most of the offensive effort, carrying 31 times for 136 yards, scoring a touchdown as well. He also added 21 more yards and a touchdown on three catches.

136 yards wouldn’t even be Green’s best day of the 2002 season. By the time he ran over the Patriots, he’d already put up a 155-yard day against the Atlanta Falcons in the season opener.

Most receiving yards – 132 (Sterling Sharpe, 1994)

You could always count on Sterling Sharpe to do great things, even in a losing effort. In 1994, the Packers came up short against the Patriots, allowing a game-winning drive and a go-ahead field goal with just seconds remaining. But Sharpe held up his end of the bargain, recording 132 yards and a touchdown on nine catches. Whatever happened down the stretch, he wasn’t to blame!

Most points scored – 18 (Brent Fullwood, 1988)

One of the most obscure names on our list today, Fullwood scored three touchdowns in a 1988 beatdown of the Patriots.

The final score was 45-3, but amusingly, Fullwood didn’t get in on the action until the Packers were already up 17-3. But a 33-yard run midway through the third quarter started the deluge, and he added touchdown runs of seven and 31 yards in the fourth quarter to get the blowout really rolling. He finished with a spectacularly efficient 118 yards and three touchdowns on 14 carries.

Sacks – 3 (Reggie White, 1996)

The Minister of Defense had famously never won a championship at any level when he joined the Green Bay Packers, but he more than did his part in Super Bowl XXXI. He took down Drew Bledsoe three times to put the game away late, including two on back to back plays to close out the third quarter.

But fans of a certain age will remember that White’s performance, great as it was, was hardly the only standout play that day. More on that in a second.

Solo tackles – 11 (Marques Anderson, 2002)

In the same game where Ahman Green ran wild in New England, Marques Anderson did plenty of work on defense. The rookie safety racked up 11 solo tackles (and an interception) to fuel a defensive effort that suffocated Tom Brady and the Patriots.

Interceptions – 2 (Ron Pitts, 1988)

Brent Fullwood did the bulk of the damage on offense in the Packers’ 1988 beatdown of the Patriots, but Ron Pitts set the table on defense. He ended two Patriots’ drives with interceptions, but he had company. The Packers intercepted Patriots quarterbacks Doug Flutie and Steve Grogan five times that day to cement the all-around blowout. 

Return yards – 248 (Desmond Howard, 1996)

We couldn’t not mention this one. Reggie White was great in Super Bowl XXXI, but Desmond Howard was transcendent. He piled up 248 total yards on kickoff and punt returns, including a 99-yard touchdown that’s etched into Packers’ lore, and was named Super Bowl MVP for his efforts.

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 9 lineup advice
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone shares his top sits and starts for Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 9 rankings. 

Starts

Dak Prescott, QB, Cowboys

at Colts

It's almost surprising that Prescott is the QB11 in fantasy points per game this year, considering he went a month without a multi-touchdown game at one point. Fortunately, he's found the end zone at least twice in each of the past two weeks. 

Now, Prescott faces a Colts team that's circling the drain before a likely selloff at the trade deadline. In its first game after dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Indy was dismantled 42-7 by the Jaguars. The Cowboys are 5.5-point favorites on the road with the fourth-highest implied point total on the week. 

Though Dak hasn't been the most reliable fantasy option this season, you can start him confidently as a top-five QB versus the Colts. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Malik Willis vs. Lions – With the Dolphins' young receiving corps getting healthy, Willis has been heating up lately as a solid fantasy streamer who offers a high floor and high ceiling. This is setting up to be a potential ceiling game for him, against a Detroit defense giving up the most fantasy points to QBs, including multiple TDs in every outing.  

  • C.J. Stroud at Chargers – Stroud has quietly had a very solid season and, with the Texans' struggles in the run game, you can expect the team to continue relying on his arm. The 25-year-old is tied for the fifth most fantasy points among quarterbacks over the last five weeks. Coming off the bye, Stroud should get a boost from Marvin Harrison Jr. getting more comfortable in the offense and Tank Dell seeing a rise in snaps. 

Chase Brown, RB, Bengals

at Falcons

Brown only finished as the RB20 in a great matchup with the Titans last week, but that would have been a top-12 fantasy back if his 20-yard touchdown catch wasn't nullified by a penalty. 

The good news is that Brown continues to dominate the Bengals backfield, playing almost 70% of the snaps last week and turning them into 20 touches, 101 scrimmage yards and eight catches. 

He also gets another positive matchup with the Falcons defense that's the fourth-easiest matchup for fantasy running backs. Atlanta has allowed seven touchdowns to RBs over its last three games and just got decimated for over 300 rushing yards by the Buccaneers backs in Week 8. 

I know it's been frustrating at times having Brown in your lineup; just don't give up now. Bigger days are within reach. If you are planning to sell him, you'll want to wait until after this game to get the most value. 

Other RBs to start:

  • Jonah Coleman at Panthers – Coleman returned from IR and immediately took control of the Broncos backfield, playing 58% of the snaps over the last two weeks and racking up 173 scrimmage yards, six receptions and a touchdown. Now, he gets a Panthers defense that's permitting the second-most fantasy points to his position. The rookie is a top-15 fantasy RB option this week. 

  • Blake Corum at Commanders – Over the last month, the Rams offense has leaned on their backfield more with Davante Adams hitting IR. That resulted in both backs averaging top-15 fantasy stats, with Corum at RB13 and Kyren Williams at RB15. Don't be misled; Williams is still the lead back and Corum hasn't played over 50% of the snaps in any game. However, he's getting plenty of opportunity, which should continue as 5.5-point favorites over the Commanders. 

  • Tyler Allgeier at Seahawks – While I hate the matchup, it's impossible to argue with the setup for Allgeier. Jeremiyah Love is on IR and Bam Knight is in concussion protocol. That leaves Allgeier as the last man standing in Arizona's RB room. Though you can't expect another 191-yard, five-catch, two-touchdown performance (because he's not playing the Cowboys defense), Allgeier can still be started as a volume-based, low-end RB2.

Justin Jefferson, WR, Vikings

vs. Bills

Jefferson isn't a name that makes it to the Start section very often because he's such a talented player that fantasy managers don't need a reminder. However, given the state of the quarterback play in Minnesota, starting Jefferson wasn't as obvious as it had been in the past. 

The veteran wideout has been held to receiving-yard totals of 55, 32, 44 and 33 in four of his last five outings and Kyler Murray wasn't finding his rhythm in Kevin O'Connell's scheme. 

Murray's new hamstring injury gave the coaching staff a chance to make a change and they jumped on it, naming Carson Wentz the starter for Monday's matchup with the Bills. With Buffalo's defense still being a work in progress, Wentz and company should be able to get the Vikings' passing game back on track. 

That's great news for Jefferson, who has averaged 6.4 receptions and 89.1 receiving yards during the seven games where Wentz has played at least 80% of the snaps over the last two seasons. That includes an 8-92-2 stat line from the opener this year. 

This move pushed Jefferson back into the top-10 fantasy WRs and in the conversation for a spot in the top-five for as long as Wentz is under center. 

Other WRs to start:

  • George Pickens at Colts – Pickens has been playing through shoulder and hamstring injuries the last couple of weeks and his playing time has taken a slight hit because of it. Jerry Jones was very clear this week that he believes Pickens needs to be getting the ball more, so this could be the rare squeaky wheel game initiated by the owner. As it stands, Pickens is still 14th in receiving yards among wideouts, but that ranking could rise thanks to a matchup with the Colts. 

  • Rashee Rice vs. Jets – For all the concerns about Rice before the season, he's actually performed well in every outing. Rice has at least 83 yards or a touchdown in all four of his healthy appearances, including a 7-53-1 stat line in his first game back last week, despite only playing 56% of the snaps. That number should rise in a favorable spot against a Jets defense that plays a lot of single-high coverage, which Rice excels against. 

  • Rome Odunze vs. Buccaneers – Odunze is 20th in receiving yards, but 53rd in fantasy points scored among wideouts. The discrepancy exists due to a lack of touchdowns, with Odunze not finding the end zone yet this season. Fortunately, the offense has been regaining its form with Caleb Williams back and Odunze has posted two of his best outings this season in recent weeks, with 69 yards against the Patriots and 87 yards versus the Seahawks. Next up is a Bucs defense that's allowed five different WRs to top 85 yards in the last month. 

Sam LaPorta, TE, Lions

at Dolphins

Through the first five weeks, LaPorta was a top-five fantasy tight end against one of the easier schedules at his position. Then came a bye, followed by back-to-back matchups against the two toughest defenses against his position: the Packers and Vikings. 

That led conspiracy theorists to speculate that the team was punishing LaPorta for his comments about being frustrated with contract extension talks with the organization. I'm guessing the degree of difficulty being turned up on him had more to do with it. 

Thankfully, a softer matchup has arrived with the Dolphins defense giving up the third-most fantasy points to tight ends. The Lions are also tied for the second-highest implied point total on the slate. This all points to a bounce-back week for LaPorta, which is why he's back in my top five. 

Other TEs to start:

  • Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Bengals – After three straight top-12 TE finishes, Pitts finally came back down to earth with just two catches for six yards in a rainy loss to the Bucs last week. Now, he suits up for a potential shoutout in the dome against a Bengals defense that's the ninth-most generous unit to tight ends. 

  • Mike Gesicki at Falcons – You can also start the other tight end in that game, with Gesicki having a great chance to extend his touchdown streak versus Atlanta. The veteran has scored a touchdown in six of his seven outings and currently sits as the TE6 in fantasy points per game. You could do worse than streaming him in a game that's tied for the highest projected point total at 52.5. 

Sits

Bryce Young, QB, Panthers

vs. Broncos

It seems like the distant past now, but Young was the QB4 overall in fantasy points per game through the first six weeks, in part thanks to an easy early-season schedule. Life comes at you fast, though and a slew of injuries on the offensive line have completely changed the outlook for this offense. It doesn't help that their last two opponents have been much tougher, the Buccaneers and Packers, leading to a test that Young ultimately failed. 

Coming off his two lowest fantasy outputs of the season, Young now has another difficult challenge ahead with the Broncos defense that got back Patrick Surtain II last week. There will be better days ahead, including the Saints matchup in Week 10, but for now, Young needs to head to your bench. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Geno Smith at Chiefs – Kansas City's defense is allowing the sixth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks and tends to be even more stout at home. Meanwhile, the Jets will be without their top receiver Garrett Wilson, who is in concussion protocol. This isn't the spot to play Smith. 

  • Baker Mayfield at Bears – At some point, Mayfield will begin throwing again and this could be the week, since he's facing a high-scoring Bears offense. But forgive me if I'm not interested in starting a quarterback who hasn't topped 13 fantasy points in a game this season and has only attempted 14 passes over the last two weeks. 

Rachaad White, RB, Commanders

vs. Rams

White came through in Week 8 thanks to a touchdown, but his usage (13 touches, 47% snap share) was disappointing given the matchup with the Eagles and the fact that Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on IR. 

The situation isn't getting better this week against a Rams defense that's his toughest opponent yet. Not only are they allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points to running backs, but it's possible Myles Garrett could be activated for the game. 

This all points to a risky setup for White, who will likely need another touchdown to save his fantasy day again. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Zach Charbonnet vs. Cardinals – The Seahawks are 8.5-point favorites, so the possibility of a goal-line carry is always there. However, it's tough to get overly excited about Charbonnet, who managed just 29 yards on nine touches while playing 37% of the snaps in his season debut. Rookie Jadarian Price displayed far more juice during the game and should earn more touches moving forward, while Charbonnet remains in a supporting role. 

  • Omarion Hampton vs. Texans – Coming off the bye, Hampton played a season-low 29.5% of the snaps. The sophomore back has only topped 56 scrimmage yards once this season. Like most of the running backs in this section, he's purely a TD-or-bust RB3. 

  • Jordan Mason vs. Bills – Mason returned to the lineup in Week 7 with a 64% snap share and 15 carries for 68 yards. Unfortunately, just one week later, those numbers dropped to 28% of the snaps and just eight carries for 20 yards. While the matchup with the Bills is a positive one, it's hard to trust Mason until we see more from him and the Vikings offense as a whole. 

Michael Wilson, WR, Cardinals

at Seahawks

Wilson finally rediscovered his ceiling with an eight-catch, 111-yard, one-touchdown performance, but it took a very friendly matchup with the Cowboys to get there. 

Wilson also accomplished the feat while playing through two broken ribs, something that will continue to be a challenge this week. 

It's also worth remembering that Wilson was held to 55 yards or less in three straight games before that springboard encounter with Dallas. The Seahawks defense, which is giving up the fewest fantasy points to wideouts, won't be the same kind of pushover. That makes Wilson a volatile WR3. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Jalen Coker vs. Broncos – The issues on the offensive line and the difficult matchup with the Broncos defense are more than enough reason to avoid Coker this week. He's only managed three catches over his last two outings. 

  • Chris Godwin Jr. at Bears – Godwin hasn't topped 50 receiving yards in a game this season and hasn't reached 40 yards in his last six appearances. Injuries have simply sapped his effectiveness, and given his age, it's likely his best days are behind him.  

  • Xavier Worthy vs. Jets – Worthy has been held to 25 yards or less in five of his seven games this season. He's also only found the end zone once all year, making him a very shaky flex option at best. 

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills

at Vikings

Kincaid's best performances have coincided with DJ Moore being in the lineup, which gives you hope that he can get back to being a top-10 fantasy tight end the rest of the way. Unfortunately, this week's matchup is with the Vikings defense, which is the biggest threat to tight ends by far this season. 

Minnesota is allowing just 5.5 fantasy points per game, with the second-place Packers coming in at 7.0 fppg. The Vikings also haven't allowed a touchdown to a tight end and we've yet to see them give up more than 65 yards to a player at the position. Even if you look back to last year, Brian Flores' crew was the eighth-worst opponent for tight ends. If Kincaid comes through this week, it will be an outlier based on what we've seen from this defense in 2026. 

Other TEs to sit:

  • Chig Okonkwo vs. Rams – After back-to-back 60-plus-yard games, Okonkwo managed just two catches for 32 yards in a tougher matchup with the Eagles last week. The Rams are the seventh most difficult opponent for fantasy tight ends, so I wouldn't get my hopes up here. 

  • Tyler Higbee at Commanders – Higbee has been held to 22 yards, 14 yards and 14 yards over his last three outings, and it's possible Terrance Ferguson could return for this contest.

item.title: Grade the trade: Ravens get much-needed quarterback help with Jacoby Brissett
item.description: The Ravens found a starting quarterback after their top two QBs suffered injuries.
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Ravens had two quarterbacks suffer injuries Sunday that sent both to injured reserve. They had to do something just to get through the rest of the season.

At the same time the Ravens were in a nightmare at Buffalo on Sunday, the Arizona Cardinals benched their starting quarterback. Jacoby Brissett was taken out late in the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys and replaced by Gardner Minshew II. Minshew led a comeback win over the Cowboys, and the Cardinals announced that Brissett would be the third-string quarterback behind Minshew and rookie Carson Beck. Brissett seemed like an obvious candidate to get traded. The Ravens were an obvious candidate to trade for a quarterback.

On Wednesday, the most obvious swap possible happened when news broke from NFL Media that the Ravens were finalizing a trade for Brissett. The final terms, via NFL Media: Arizona gets a fourth-round pick in 2027 and a seventh-round pick in 2028, while the Ravens get Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. The Cardinals also paid a little more than half of Brissett’s remaining salary this season to facilitate the deal, NFL Media said.

But at least the Ravens have a viable option for the rest of the season.

Ravens get Jacoby Brissett

The truth of the NFL is teams don't want to trade their starting quarterbacks or their backup quarterbacks either. It's rare that a team has a third-string quarterback that can come in and start right way for another team. The price the Ravens paid wasn’t too egregious, with a pick swap in the mid rounds and a seventh-round pick in two years.

The Ravens were never going to find a quarterback who can completely save their season, but Brissett will at least allow them to run a competent offense. Brissett was the Cardinals' starter for most of the past two seasons and threw for 5,085 yards with 33 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. That didn't lead to many wins for Arizona, but the Cardinals don't have a good supporting cast. The Ravens are in much better shape. And Brissett can at least get the ball to playmakers like Zay Flowers.

Nobody should believe Brissett will save Baltimore's season and help them win the division. The Ravens are 4-4 and will be starting undrafted rookie Fagnano against a good Jaguars team on Thursday. But Brissett was the best option available, and he at least makes sure the Ravens aren't playing out the string with uncompetitive football for two months. And maybe a miracle happens and the Ravens are still in contention by the time Jackson returns — if he can.

Grade: B-

Cardinals ship off a quarterback

The Cardinals probably knew, when they made Brissett their third-string quarterback on Monday, that he wouldn't be with the team by the end of the week.

It's a perfectly reasonable move. The Cardinals are going to start Beck soon to get a look at him by next season. Minshew can do as well as Brissett in the short term. They get a decent mid-round pick swap and a future seventh for a player who wasn't going to see the field the rest of the season and has an expiring contract. They also allow Brissett a chance to play meaningful football the rest of the season after serving as their starter for most of the past two seasons.

It's not an overly meaningful move for the franchise, but fine for the Cardinals for getting a deal done quickly.

Grade: C+

item.title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
item.description: Here are all of the NFL trade deadline news and rumors surrounding our Denver Broncos. The deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2pm mountain.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline, but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add.

Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense.

The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else?

Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way.

As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far.

We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days.

item.title: Kadyn Proctor will play against Detroit Lions in Week 9
item.description: Proctor cleared concussion protocol and will play for Dolphins against Lions.
item.content:encoded:
Miami Dolphins’ starting left guard, rookie Kadyn Proctor, missed the team’s week 8 contest against the New England Patriots due to a concussion the young player suffered the previous week in a win over the New York Jets. According to Miami’s head coach, Jeff Hafley, Proctor will return to the team’s starting lineup this Sunday when Miami hosts the Detroit Lions.

Speaking with the South Florida media on Friday, Hafley said, “Proctor is clear,” when asked about the rookie’s availability for Sunday’s game.

In his absence, Miami’s offensive line struggled against a stout Patriots front — allowing 5 sacks and managing just 74 yards rushing on 20 attempts (just 3.7 yards per carry).

Proctor’s return against the Lions provides a bit of intrigue — as Detroit was heavily rumored to be big fans of the Alabama product coming out of college. Numerous mock drafts had the Lions taking him with the 17th pick in the 1st round of the 2026 NFL Draft — before Dolphins’ general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan pounced and took Proctor with the 12th pick. The Lions settled for right tackle Blake Miller out of Clemson.

We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the team looks to secure their second victory on the season when they host Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and the rest of the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
