The latest Kansas City Chiefs news

Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, claims he owes over $3.45M in debts | ESPN

In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in “deferred compensation.” The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property.

Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for “individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors,” according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt.

The documents claim Rice’s largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit.

The NFL trade deadline is nearing. Here’s what the Chiefs need to solve | The Kansas City Star

Well, it’s absent again in his absence. A month later, that aforementioned completion in Week 4 against the Raiders remains the most recent time the Chiefs have completed a pass downfield (defined as targeted receiver more than 20 yards beyond the line of scrimmage).

They have played three full games without him. In those games, Mahomes is 0 for 5 when targeting a receiver deep into the secondary.

Chiefs Announce Legend Kendall Gammon As 2026 Salute to Service Award Nominee | The Mothership

Following a 15-year NFL career, Gammon has used his experiences with adversity, mental health challenges and the transition from professional football to connect with veterans navigating similar challenges after military service.

“I am truly honored to be nominated as the Kansas City Chiefs representative for the Salute to Service Award,” Gammon said. “It means so much to have the opportunity to support service members, veterans, and their families who have given so much in service to our country. Connecting with Kansas City’s military community has been incredibly meaningful and has allowed me to stay close to Chiefs Kingdom in a special way.”

Chris Jones Has an Interesting Explanation for Chiefs’ Frustrating Sack Drought | Sports Illustrated

During a media appearance on Wednesday, Jones reiterated why he believes the sacks will eventually come.

“It’s all about perspective from my angle. We’ve got 10 games [left], right?” Jones said. “So, continue to chop wood. This year is an awkward year for all of us. Sacks started off slow, but you’ve got to continue to do what you’ve been doing. Eventually, they’re going to start coming, and when they come, they come in bunches.”

Jets expected to get star RB back for matchup with Chiefs | KCTV5

New York Jets star running back Breece Hall has been sidelined for weeks due to a quad injury.

This week, as his team is poised to come to the Midwest, the Wichita, Kansas, native and Iowa State product is expected to return to action.

Hall practiced in full Thursday and is expected to suit up for Sunday’s game between the 2-6 Jets and 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs.

It would be Hall’s first game since Week 3 of this season.

Around the NFL

Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars roll past Ravens. Is Jacksonville now the AFC team to beat? | The Athletic

Are the Jaguars the most complete team in the entire AFC right now?

Yes. The Jaguars check just about every box you would want in a contender. They didn’t capitalize on as many opportunities as they could have against Baltimore, but they still have an offense that’s capable of scoring on big plays and grinding out tough yards.

They have a defense that can get after the quarterback and generate turnovers. Not only do the Jaguars lead the NFL in point margin, they also went into Thursday tied for first with a plus-7 turnover margin.

Vikings to start Carson Wentz vs. Bills on Monday with Kyler Murray battling hamstring injury | NFL.com

Max Brosmer will assume backup duties behind Wentz on Monday, O’Connell added.

The starting lineup swap doesn’t come as a surprise after O’Connell told reporters on Monday that Murray was dealing with a “sore” hamstring following their Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions.

Murray has had a challenging start to the 2026 season — his first in Minnesota. With Murray behind center for the majority of the season, the Vikings’ offense has struggled mightily, ranking 29th in yards gained per game, 31st in passing and 27th in points scored per contest (20).

Brandon Aiyuk to return to 49ers’ facility Friday afternoon, reportedly discussing forfeiture of $13 million bonus | Yahoo! Sports

In June, Aiyuk continued to publicly ask the team to cut him so he could sign somewhere else, specifically the Washington Commanders. But that wasn’t going to be possible until he was reinstated from the the reserve/left squad, where he landed because he failed to show up for mandatory team activities, including training camp.

In a video, the receiver said that he would never step foot in the 49ers’ facility again; he also claimed that he had fired his agent.

Now, with Rosenhaus leading Aiyuk’s negotiations, the receiver will hope to finally get his new start elsewhere, assuming the 49ers trade or cut him.

item.title: Scouting the Enemy: Carolina Panthers
item.description: The Denver Broncos battle the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Here is a deeper look at their Week 9 opponent.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos will battle Carolina Panthers on Sunday. It’s a huge matchup for the Broncos who have a shot to keep their winning streak alive and enter their bye week with a 7-2 record if they are victorious. Here is a deeper look at their Week 9 opponent.

2025 Carolina Panthers Regular Season Review

The Carolina Panthers won the NFC South with an 8-9 record in Head Coach Dave Canales’ second season leading the team.. They lost to the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card Round 34-31.

2026 Carolina Panthers Offseason Additions and Departures

After securing their first division title since the 2017 season, the Carolina Panthers made a few big splashes in free agency to be more competitive in 2026. The two high-profile signings came on defense. They signed edge rusher Jaelan Phillips to a four-year, $120 million dollar contract. The Panthers also inked All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd to a three-year, $45 million dollar contract.

Carolina didn’t have many big-named departures. However, they parted ways with two starters. Defensive lineman A’Shawn Robinson and offensive lineman Austin Corbettt, whose time with the Panthers was marred by injuries.

In the 2026 NFL Draft, they made bolstering their trenches a priority. They took Georgia tackle Monroe Freeling in the first round and Texas Tech defensive tackle Lee Hunter in the second. Both have been starters for them this season. Tennessee wide receiver Chris Brazzell II was their third-round pick. Unfortunately, his rookie season ended early after suffering a torn LCL in summer.

On the bright side, their Day 3 group of talent has earned plenty of playing time. They snagged two starters on Day 3 with Texas A&M cornerback Will Lee and Penn State safety Zakee Wheatley. Fifth-round offensive lineman Sam Hecht and seventh-round linebacker Jackson Kuwatch have earned backup roles and are playing on special teams for them this season.

Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Bryce Young

As noted above, the Panthers made improving their defense a big part of their free agent plans. On offense, they banked on the progression of quarterback Bryce Young to be the catalyst that would take their offense to the next level. He is my X-Factor for them on offense.

It’s been an up-and-down season for Young. Even so, the Panthers have had a big turnaround on offense. They are a Top 10 unit in the NFL by most metrics. Wide receivers Tetairoa McMillian and Jalen Coker have been very productive. Tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller have gotten their fair share of looks in the passing game too.

Young has done a great job diving up his targets and despite a less-than-optimal completion percentage. In seven starts, Young is completing 59-percent of his passes, thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and has just 5 interceptions on the season. He is doing great on first down and is moving the chains early and often. However, his third down efficiency has been less than optimal.

A big reason for that is poor play from their offensive line. In just seven games, Young has been sack almost as many times as he was in 2025. This is a game where Denver’s defensive front seven needs to make an impact. While their sack total isn’t nearly as good as it was last season, they’re still a top-ranked team when it comes to generating pressure and getting quarterback hits. If they can rattle Young, I like Denver’s odds of winning this game.

Defensive X-Factor: Linebacker Devin Lloyd

The Panthers made some splashes in free agency to upgrade their defense. Alas, it has been their biggest weakness to date. No excuses can be made, but they have had a bunch of injuries. Their poor play and inconsistency led to the firing of Ejiro Evero at the end of October. Broncos Country may remember that name, as Evero was the Defensive Coordinator for the Broncos in 2022 when Nathaniel Hackett was Head Coach.

One bright spot for them on defense has been linebacker Devin Lloyd. He’s my X-Factor for them on defense. Lloyd had a Pro-Bowl and All-Pro season in his fourth and final year with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. He notched 135 tackles, 5 interceptions, and 1.5 sacks.

This season, he has continued to play at a high level. The fifth-year pro already has 69 tackles, 2 interceptions, and 2 sacks on the season. If there is any player on defense Denver’s offense needs to be cognizant of, it’s Lloyd. He has incredible range and playmaking ability. Whether it’s against the run or the pass, he is one of the league’s most versatile defenders that can make a huge impact on the game.

How the Broncos can achieve a victory over thePanthers

ICYMI: Yesterday, I wrote how the Broncos can achieve their seventh victory of the season over the Panthers. Overall, this is a game where I really like Denver’s chances. If they can establish the run on offense and get after Young defensively, they should be able to come away with a big win before the bye week.

Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 30, Panthers 17.
